case_name: R. C. Sood v High Court of Judicature At Rajasthan and Others
respondent: High Court of Judicature At Rajasthan
facts: The petitioner who was a member of the Rajasthan Higher Judicial Service, has by this petition under Article 32 of the Constitution of India, assailed the disciplinary proceedings which have been initiated against him pursuant to the resolution dated 5th May, 1995 of the Full Court of the Rajasthan High Court.
The petitioner had joined the Rajasthan Higher Judicial Service as a District and Sessions Judge on 31 July 1976.

He had been posted and had discharged duties at various places and in different capacities including that as an Additional Registrar, Rajasthan High Court and Registrar (Vigilance), Rajasthan High Court.
With effect from 1st July, 1989 to 1 February 1994 the petitioner was posted as Registrar of the Rajasthan High Court.

After he was posted as District and Sessions Judge, Jodhpur on 02 February 1994 and then was transferred as District and Sessions Judge, Jaipur with effect from 6th June, 1994 but before his superannuation on attaining the age of 58 years, departmental enquiries were initiated against him on two occasions.
The first departmental enquiry was initiated by a resolution of Full Court dated 21 October 1994, which was challenged by the petitioner by filling a writ petition in this Court.

By order dated 22 November 1994 in the judgment reported as R.C. Sood Vs. High Court of Rajasthan, 1994 (Suppl) 3 SCC 711 1994 Indlaw SC 1201, this Court quashed the said disciplinary proceedings and the Full Court's resolution in respect thereto.
The second disciplinary proceeding, which has been challenged in this writ petition, has been initiated by the High Court vide its resolution dated 5/6 January 1995.

Rule nisi was issued by this Court limited to the question of legality of the initiation of disciplinary proceedings against the petitioner and not on the question of his retirement on his attaining the age of 58 years.
issues: Whether the impugned resolution dated 5/6 January, 1995 is legal and valid
Whether the departmental enquiry initiated by the High Court vide its resolution dated 5/6 January, 1995 is lawful
petitioner_arguments: The petitioner's troubles did not end with the quashing of the first disciplinary proceedings.
The impugned resolution and the subsequent departmental enquiry are an attempt to thwart the petitioner's prospects in his judicial career.
respondent_arguments: The respondents have taken a view that the complaint against the petitioner is false and fabricated.
The respondents have also taken a view that the petitioner has been proceeded against on certain other charges.
court_reasoning: It was difficult to appreciate how the Two Judge Committee could come to the conclusion that there was a forgery in the record and/or that any person had benefited from the said error or that the petitioner was responsible for the same.
The Court has held that it is necessary to first refer to the set of facts pertaining to the issuance of the first disciplinary proceedings as that has every material bearing in the present case.
holding: The impugned resolution dated 5/6 January, 1995 and the subsequent departmental enquiry are quashed.
The petitioner's troubles did not end with the quashing of the first disciplinary proceedings.
cases_cited: R. C. Sood v High Court of Judicature At Rajasthan
in the judgment reported as R.C. Sood Vs. High Court of Rajasthan
